SKIN & SPECIAL SENSES__Skin (epidermis,:
Overview — Three Layers

Skin has an epidermis (keratinised stratified squamous epithelium), a dermis (connective tissue) and a hypodermis (subcutaneous fat).

🔬 Image slot — skin showing epidermal layers, dermis and hypodermis
Epidermal Layers ⭐

From base to surface (mnemonic "Come, Let's Get Sun Burnt"):

LayerFeature
Stratum basaleDividing stem cells (keratinocytes) + melanocytes + Merkel cells
Stratum spinosum'Prickle' cells joined by desmosomes; Langerhans cells
Stratum granulosumKeratohyalin granules
Stratum lucidumClear layer — only in thick (palmoplantar) skin
Stratum corneumDead, flattened, keratin-filled cells (barrier)
Non-keratinocytes: melanocytes (melanin, basal), Langerhans cells (antigen presentation, spinosum), Merkel cells (touch, basal).
Dermis & Hypodermis
  • Papillary dermis (loose CT, dermal papillae) + reticular dermis (dense irregular CT — collagen & elastic strength)
  • Contains vessels, nerves, appendages (follicles, glands) and sensory receptors (Meissner's, Pacinian corpuscles)
  • Hypodermis = subcutaneous adipose + loose CT (insulation, energy, cushioning)
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Skin cancers
BCC (basal cells), SCC (keratinocytes, keratin pearls), melanoma (melanocytes, S100).
Psoriasis
Epidermal hyperplasia + parakeratosis; thickened stratum corneum.
Blistering disorders
Pemphigus (desmosomes, intra-epidermal) vs pemphigoid (hemidesmosomes, sub-epidermal).
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Epidermis (base→surface): basale → spinosum → granulosum → (lucidum, thick skin only) → corneum.
  • Non-keratinocytes: melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells.
  • Dermis = papillary (loose) + reticular (dense irregular); receptors: Meissner (touch, papillae), Pacinian (pressure, deep).
  • Cancers: BCC, SCC (keratin pearls), melanoma (S100); pemphigus = intra-epidermal, pemphigoid = sub-epidermal.
SKIN & SPECIAL SENSES__Hair Follicle & S:
Overview — The Pilosebaceous Unit

A hair follicle plus its sebaceous gland and arrector pili muscle form the pilosebaceous unit.

🔬 Image slot — hair follicle with bulb, sebaceous gland and arrector pili muscle
  • Hair follicle: an epidermal downgrowth; the bulb (matrix cells) grows the hair around a vascular dermal papilla
  • Sebaceous gland: secretes sebum by the holocrine mechanism (whole cell disintegrates) into the follicle
  • Arrector pili: smooth muscle that erects the hair ('goosebumps') and helps express sebum
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Acne vulgaris
Follicle plugging + sebum + Cutibacterium acnes → inflamed pilosebaceous units.
Sebaceous cyst
Blocked follicle/gland → keratin-filled cyst.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Pilosebaceous unit = follicle + sebaceous gland + arrector pili.
  • Sebaceous glands secrete sebum by holocrine secretion (whole cell disintegrates).
  • Hair grows from the matrix cells of the bulb around the dermal papilla; arrector pili = 'goosebumps'.
SKIN & SPECIAL SENSES__Sweat Glands:
Overview — Two Types
🔬 Image slot — coiled eccrine sweat gland in the deep dermis with secretory coil and duct
EccrineApocrine
WhereAll over the body (palms/soles/forehead richest)Axilla, groin, areola
Opens ontoSkin surface (own pore)Into the hair follicle
SecretionWatery sweat (merocrine) → thermoregulationViscous, odour when bacteria act on it (despite the name, uses merocrine/apocrine); active from puberty
CellsSecretory coil (clear + dark cells) + myoepithelial cells; duct reabsorbs Na⁺Larger lumen; myoepithelial cells
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Cystic fibrosis
CFTR defect → failure to reabsorb duct Cl⁻/Na⁺ → salty sweat (sweat test).
Hyperhidrosis
Excess eccrine sweating.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Eccrine = everywhere, watery, thermoregulation, opens on the skin; apocrine = axilla/groin, opens into the follicle, from puberty.
  • Both have myoepithelial cells; the eccrine duct reabsorbs sodium.
  • Cystic fibrosis → salty sweat (CFTR-based sweat test).
SKIN & SPECIAL SENSES__Eye (retina, corn:
Overview — Three Coats

The eye has three layers: outer fibrous (sclera + cornea), middle vascular/uvea (choroid, ciliary body, iris) and inner neural (retina).

🔬 Image slot — retina layers (photoreceptors, bipolar, ganglion cells) and cornea
Key Structures ⭐
  • Cornea: transparent, avascular; layers = epithelium (stratified squamous) → Bowman's → stroma (ordered collagen) → Descemet's → endothelium (pumps water out to stay clear)
  • Lens: transparent, avascular; crystallin-filled lens fibres; a capsule; suspended by zonules from the ciliary body (accommodation)
  • Retina: light passes through inner layers to reach the photoreceptors (rods & cones) at the back → bipolar cells → ganglion cells (axons form the optic nerve). The fovea (cones) = sharpest vision; the optic disc = blind spot
  • Retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) supports photoreceptors
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Cataract
Lens opacification (crystallin changes).
Macular degeneration / retinopathy
Photoreceptor/RPE loss; diabetic microvascular damage.
Retinal detachment
Separation of neural retina from RPE.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Three coats: fibrous (sclera/cornea) → uvea (choroid/ciliary/iris) → retina.
  • Cornea is avascular; its endothelium pumps water out to stay transparent.
  • Retina: light → through inner layers → photoreceptors (rods/cones) → bipolar → ganglion cells (optic nerve); fovea = cones/acuity; optic disc = blind spot.
  • Cataract = lens opacity.
SKIN & SPECIAL SENSES__Ear (cochlea, org:
Overview

The inner ear's cochlea converts sound vibrations into nerve signals; the sensory apparatus is the organ of Corti.

🔬 Image slot — cochlear cross-section with the three scalae and the organ of Corti
  • The cochlea has three fluid-filled ducts: scala vestibuli & scala tympani (perilymph) and the middle scala media / cochlear duct (endolymph)
  • The organ of Corti sits on the basilar membrane: hair cells with stereocilia touching the tectorial membrane
  • Sound → basilar-membrane vibration → stereocilia bend → hair cells depolarise → cochlear nerve
  • Different frequencies stimulate different points along the basilar membrane (tonotopy: base = high, apex = low)
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
Sensorineural deafness
Hair-cell loss (noise, age/presbycusis, ototoxic drugs).
Ménière's disease
Endolymphatic hydrops → vertigo, tinnitus, hearing loss.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Sound is transduced by hair cells of the organ of Corti on the basilar membrane (stereocilia bend against the tectorial membrane).
  • Three scalae: vestibuli & tympani (perilymph), media/cochlear duct (endolymph).
  • Tonotopy: base = high frequency, apex = low; hair-cell loss → sensorineural deafness.
SKIN & SPECIAL SENSES__Olfactory Epithel:
Overview — The Epithelium of Smell

Olfactory epithelium in the roof of the nasal cavity is a tall pseudostratified epithelium containing the sensory neurons for smell.

🔬 Image slot — olfactory epithelium: bipolar olfactory neurons, supporting & basal cells, Bowman's glands
CellRole
Olfactory (bipolar) neuronsThe receptors; non-motile cilia bind odorants; axons form CN I. Uniquely regenerate from basal cells
Supporting (sustentacular) cellsColumnar support cells
Basal cellsStem cells (replace olfactory neurons)
Bowman's glands secrete serous fluid that dissolves odorants so they can be sensed.
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Olfactory epithelium = pseudostratified; receptors are bipolar neurons (CN I) that regenerate.
  • Bowman's glands dissolve odorants; supporting + basal cells complete the epithelium.
SKIN & SPECIAL SENSES__Taste Buds:
Overview — The Receptors of Taste

Taste buds are barrel-shaped clusters of cells within the epithelium of the tongue papillae, opening to the surface via a taste pore.

🔬 Image slot — taste buds within a circumvallate papilla, each with a taste pore
  • Located in fungiform, foliate and circumvallate papillae (not the filiform papillae)
  • Cell types: gustatory (taste receptor) cells + supporting cells + basal (stem) cells
  • Detect five modalities: sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami
  • Innervated by cranial nerves VII (anterior tongue), IX (posterior), X (epiglottis)
⭐ Exam Pearls
  • Taste buds = barrel-shaped, in fungiform/foliate/circumvallate papillae, with a taste pore.
  • Gustatory cells detect 5 tastes; innervated by CN VII, IX, X.
  • Basal cells continually regenerate the receptor cells.
